thread:
PagerDuty Bot: :rotating_light: Alert: production-streaming p99 latency > 3.5s for the last 2m (current: 4.2s). Trigger: p99_latency_threshold. Incident ID: INC-9370

oncall_natalie: saw the page, I'm on it. pulling metrics now.

sre_priya: i'm looking at the real-time dashboard — p95 ~ 600ms, p99 jumped to 4.2s, request rate steady. Streaming stalls correlate with long KV cache misses.

eng_runtime_elena: can you paste the node-level breakdown? suspecting a handful of GPU workers.

sre_priya: here — top tail hosts: gpu-node-045, gpu-node-047 showing p99 spikes.

infra_tim: checking telemetry: gpu-node-045 ECC correctable errors incrementing, thermal sensor TMP_GFX at 88C and fan RPM oscillating between 2200-4200. looks like thermal throttling.

oncall_natalie: tagging platform team, @eng-runtime and @infra. Can we evacuate that host now?

eng_runtime_elena: recommend immediate drain of node-045 and failover. starting graceful drain: `kubectl drain gpu-node-045 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` and switching routing policy for streaming to avoid bursting more nodes.

infra_tim: running `gcloud compute ssh gpu-node-045 -- sudo nvidia-smi -q` — visible ECC Correctable: +12 in last 5m, clip levels show reduced clock speeds (throttle). driver logs show: `thermal throttling engaged`.

sre_priya: putting mitigation in place: adjust autoscaler to pre-warm extra capacity and apply temporary routing to dedicated fallback pool (lower-throughput but stable). Also reducing batching: set `max_batch_size` to 32 for streaming model to lower tail amplification.

support_mike: any customer-facing impact? are calls failing or just slower?

oncall_natalie: early assessment: ~0.6% of streaming sessions saw stalls >5s, sporadic 502s from worker OOM retries. not widespread but visible for high-concurrency tenants.

product_oliver: flagging potential customer severity — QA: prepare a short notification if we see customer-visible errors persist >30m.

eng_runtime_elena: drain complete for gpu-node-045, pods rescheduled. routing confirmed: requests to that AZ now hitting fallback pool. p99 dropped to ~1.1s immediately after drain, p95 stable.

hw_lead_rafael: requesting physical check on node-045 hardware — scheduling on-call hardware swap. suspect fan assembly or heatsink contact.

infra_tim: as a precaution, quarantining gpu-node-047 for inspection too — it shows early signs of the same pattern (TMP_GFX ~82C, ECC+3).

oncall_natalie: creating incident timeline and customer impact note. current mitigation: drained nodes 045/047 + routing to fallback + batch reduction. monitoring for 15m window.

sre_priya: monitoring logs for streaming stalls. one more thing: KV cache churn spiked during failover — increasing local cache TTLs to reduce upstream pressure.

support_mike: logging a support ticket for the 2 customers who reported stalls during 14:12-14:18 PST. adding details and mitigation steps.

product_oliver: agree on notification if any SLAs materially breached; status page updated to: `partial_degradation` with message 'Some streaming sessions experienced increased latency; mitigations in progress.'

infra_tim: healthcheck: p99 now at 0.9-1.2s after mitigations, no new ECC surges.

oncall_natalie: handing off to next on-call (sre_priya -> oncall_natalie_endorse). next_oncall: @sre_priya until 18:00 UTC. Please kick off postmortem and RCA ticket.

eng_runtime_elena: note for RCA: investigate KV cache eviction policy under rapid reschedule, improve graceful degrade route to CPU variant earlier to avoid queues, and add hardware backoff to scheduling when ECC rate > threshold.

hw_lead_rafael: will coordinate hardware replacement for node-045 tomorrow (RMA for GPU unit) and run thermal validation on replacement.

noncall_natalie: incident moving to monitoring state. followups: RCA ticket INC-9370-RCA, customer comms draft in #support-drafts. closing alert on pager. :white_check_mark:

PagerDuty Bot: Incident INC-9370 status changed: mitigated -> monitoring.

sre_priya: quick post-incident tasks: add runbook step to auto-quarantine nodes with ECC slope > 5/min, wire alert to flag fan RPM oscillation, and add a streaming fallback test to chaos suite.

support_mike: thanks all — will update affected customers with timeline and workaround.

product_oliver: ping product ops for follow-up review tomorrow.

oncall_natalie: thanks team. I archived logs and saved relevant dashboards to the incident folder: https://internal.incidents/INC-9370/logs.

sre_priya: good job everyone. final last check: p99 holding at ~1.0s for 10m, leaving in monitoring for 30m then close. :thumbsup:
